title: Arithmetic nodal model, coefficient projection and origin predicate
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For $a\in R$, write $A(R,a)=R[x_0,x_1]/(x_0x_1-a)$ for the existing nodal chart algebra [def-trf-strict-semistable-curve, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Define $\operatorname{constant}(R,a,c)$ to be the class of $c\in R$, and $\operatorname{coordinate}(R,a,i)$ to be the class of $x_i$ for $i\in\{0,1\}$. For $\pi\in R$, define $\operatorname{originIdeal}(R,a,\pi)=(\overline{x_0},\overline{x_1},\overline{\pi})\subset A(R,a)$. For every integer $n\geq0$ put $M_n(R,\pi)=\operatorname{Spec}A(R,\pi^n)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and define its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ to be the spectrum morphism induced by the inclusion of coefficients $R\to A(R,\pi^n)$. For a point $o\in M_n(R,\pi)$ define $\operatorname{IsOrigin}(R,\pi,n,o)$ to mean that the prime ideal corresponding to $o$ is exactly $\operatorname{originIdeal}(R,\pi^n,\pi)$. This is a predicate, not an assertion that this ideal is prime for arbitrary $R,\pi,n$; no point is chosen. In the arithmetic nodal situation it specifies the point $(\pi,x_0,x_1)$ without adding residue-field data.
